BUILT TO UNDERSTAND

Beyond a prediction.

A reproducible ML project, from raw data to a usable screening tool.

01 / THE PROBLEM

Convincing offers can hide harmful requests.

OfferGuard helps job seekers inspect recruitment text before responding. It extracts warning signs and offers independent verification steps. It does not authenticate offers.

Why this problem matters ↗
02 / THE APPROACH

Two kinds of evidence, kept distinct.

A TF-IDF logistic regression model learns word patterns. Separate policy checks find explicit payment requests, personal-account transfers, pressure and identity requests. Short or unfamiliar text triggers abstention from the model.

03 / ENGINEERING

Python training. Browser inference.

Learned weights and vocabulary are exported to JSON. Browser predictions are checked against Python fixtures. Input text stays on the device; no API key or language model subscription is needed.

Source, tests & training code on GitHub ↗
04 / WHAT COMES NEXT

The ambition needs fresh evidence.

Collect consented, recent examples. Build a blinded evaluation across platforms. Add independently sourced company and recruiter verification. Measure whether users make better decisions. These stages are planned, not completed.

How to read the code.

Start with ml/text.py (preprocessing shared with the browser), then ml/train.py (grouped split, TF-IDF, calibration and threshold selection) and finally dist/assets/engine.js (browser inference and evidence rules). A model that always predicts “legitimate” scores 95% accuracy while catching zero scams, which is why the report focuses on recall, precision and false alarms.
